slides.title: Quiz item 1
slides.html:
Triangle JKL ≅ triangle VUW. Name the angle that matches angle L and the side that matches KJ.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

L matches W, so the angle is angle W. K matches U and J matches V, so the side is UV.

Reveal second check

Reverse the lists VUW and JKL: W returns to L and UV returns to KJ.

slides.title: Quiz item 2
slides.html:
Triangle NOP ≅ triangle ZYX, NP = 4t + 5, and ZX = 37. Find t.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

N matches Z and P matches X, so NP = ZX. Then 4t + 5 = 37, so 4t = 32 and t = 8.

Reveal second check

Substitute: 4(8)+5=37. Both first-to-third sides have length 37.

slides.title: Quiz item 3
slides.html:
RS = XY = 7, RT = XZ = 11, and angle SRT = angle YXZ = 46 degrees. Prove triangle RST ≅ triangle XYZ. Then name the side equal to ST.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

RS=XY and RT=XZ are given. The equal angles are included, so RST≅XYZ by SAS. ST=YZ by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

R↔X, S↔Y, T↔Z; the paired sides meet at R and X, exactly the marked angle vertices.

geo.check: R↔X, S↔Y, T↔Z; the paired sides meet at R and X, exactly the marked angle vertices.

slides.title: Quiz item 4
slides.html:
In triangles EFG and LMN, angle F = angle M = 52 degrees, angle G = angle N = 61 degrees, and FG = MN = 9. Which test we have proved shows the triangles are congruent? Explain where the side is.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

ASA proves EFG≅LMN. FG and MN join the two given angle vertices, so they are included sides.

Reveal second check

Map F to M and G to N; the endpoint rays then determine E and L uniquely on the chosen side.

slides.title: Quiz item 5
slides.html:
Segments PR and QS cross at H. H is the midpoint of each one, PH = 6, and QH = 10. Prove triangle PHQ ≅ triangle RHS. Then find RH and SH.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

RH=PH=6 and SH=QH=10 by midpoint. Angle PHQ=RHS by vertical angles. Hence PHQ≅RHS by SAS.

Reveal second check

The half-turn about H sends P to R and Q to S, giving an independent motion check of the same correspondence.

slides.title: Quiz item 6
slides.html:
Triangle UVW ≅ triangle KML, UW = 2r + 9, and KL = 35. Use CPCTC to find r.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

U↔K and W↔L, so UW=KL. Thus 2r+9=35, 2r=26, r=13.

Reveal second check

2(13)+9=35; read first-to-third positions in both ordered triples.

slides.title: Quiz item 7
slides.html:
In triangle DEF, DE = DF. Angle E = (5z + 1) degrees and angle F = (3z + 19) degrees. Find z and both base angles.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Equal legs give angle E=angle F, so 5z+1=3z+19, 2z=18, z=9. Each base angle is 46 degrees.

Reveal second check

5(9)+1=46 and 3(9)+19=46. Both are positive and less than 90; no angle sum is used in the student solution.

slides.title: Quiz item 8
slides.html:
In triangle JKL, angle JLK = angle LKJ, JL = 6s - 7, and JK = 4s + 9. Explain why the two named sides are equal, then find s.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

The converse isosceles theorem gives JL=JK. Solve 6s-7=4s+9, 2s=16, s=8; both sides are 41.

Reveal second check

6(8)-7=41=4(8)+9. Independently compare JLK and JKL: equal base angles and LK=KL give ASA, then CPCTC.

slides.title: Quiz item 9
slides.html:
Triangles BCD and RST have matching angles B = R = 31, C = S = 67 and D = T = 82 degrees. Side CD is 4 and side ST is 10. A student says AAA proves triangle BCD ≅ triangle RST. Use the givens to show the student is wrong.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

That match would need CD = ST, but CD = 4 and ST = 10. Equal angles do not force congruence.

Reveal second check

All three angle sizes are distinct, so any congruence must match equal-sized angles in exactly this order. No alternative vertex matching rescues the claim.

slides.title: Quiz item 10
slides.html:
You are given AC = BC and angle ACD = angle BCD. Put these three proof lines in order and give the reason for line (iii): (i) AD = BD by CPCTC; (ii) triangle ACD ≅ triangle BCD by SAS; (iii) CD = CD.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

First (iii), because a segment equals itself. Combine it with the two givens to obtain (ii), by SAS. Only then conclude (i), by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

C is the included-angle vertex between AC and CD, and between BC and CD. The CPCTC line now has its congruence hypothesis established.

geo.check: C is the included-angle vertex between AC and CD, and between BC and CD. The CPCTC line now has its congruence hypothesis established.

slides.html: 1. What's confusing?
